correctness.rationale: The interval 0≤x≤1 is forward invariant, x is positive at finite time, and g is monotone. If g were unbounded, once δg≥2β the exponential bound on x would make the remaining gain integral finite, a contradiction. Finite g∞ gives integrability of x² and bounded x′, hence x→0; the log equation excludes g∞<β/δ. Before threshold set y=β/δ−g and z=x/y. Direct differentiation gives dz/dt=x(δ−βz+αz²); in time τ with τ′=y this is dz/dτ=zQ(z), Q(z)=δ−βz+αz². For Δ≥0 and z₀≤z₊ the sign chart (including the double root) keeps z between positive bounds; (1/y)′=αz² then precludes a finite crossing, makes y comparable to 1/t and implies τ→∞. The attracting or fixed projective root gives both recorded constants by integration and averaging. In the remaining cases Q>0 along the increasing z branch. As z→∞ the integral of d log x/dz=(δ−βz)/(zQ(z)) converges, so x→x_*>0 and y→0. The physical travel time integral ∫dz/[xQ(z)] is finite, and g′>0 there makes the crossing strict. The logarithmic exponential rate follows by averaging (log x)′. The invariant ray gives the recorded equality solution, and both same-parameter seeds are on the claimed sides. The supplied finite checks were inspected, not executed; they are not used as proofs of extinction or strict asymptotic separation.
